evidence.description: Two removed wooden fastener-like pieces are shown by hand and side by side. One is distinctly longer; both have a bent/curved shaft and enlarged head.
Reported workshop explanation: possibly two per Kumpf, one long and one short, potentially used to establish or secure twist/inclination.

candidates.statement: Each Kumpf uses a paired long and short wooden securing pin.
The length/curvature difference contributes to Kumpf inclination or twist.
The pins primarily secure the Kumpf and do not set its geometry.
Long/short pairs vary by repair history rather than being a canonical pair.

saturday_acceptance: Photograph long and short pin together while still installed on at least three Kumpf assemblies.
Record orientation, head side, insertion direction and neighboring paddle/rim reference.
Keep each removed pair physically associated with its Kumpf ID.
Measure total length, section, bend/offset and head geometry of each removed pin.
Photograph empty seats/holes immediately after removal.
Measure Kumpf inclination before removal and compare against long/short pair orientation.
Ask experienced craftsperson what local term is correct and what functional difference long vs short has.
promotion_rule: Do not promote pair count or inclination-setting function to current geometry until installed evidence and craft explanation agree.
